title: The Cost of Overfitting: Lessons Traders Can Learn From Data Science
partialText: Overfitting happens when trading strategies are optimized too closely to historical data, mistaking noise for signal. While backtests may look impressive, overfit systems often collapse in live markets. By applying data science principles like in-sample/out-of-sample testing, cross-validation, simpler rule design, and probabilistic thinking, traders can build more resilient, adaptable strategies.

title: Reflections of a Living Soul
partialText: In Chapter VIII of The Picture of Dorian Gray, Dorian awakens to a beautiful morning but is haunted by his portrait’s mysterious transformation, reflecting his soul’s corruption. He writes to Sibyl Vane seeking forgiveness, only to learn of her tragic death. Lord Henry consoles him with his cynical view of love and society. Dorian resolves to embrace eternal youth and secret pleasures, leaving morality to the portrait.

title: The Cynicism Influence of Lord Henry
partialText: Dorian Gray experiences heartbreak as Sibyl Vane’s acting fails on stage, shattering his idealized vision of her. Haunted by his portrait’s subtle cruelty, he reflects on love, art, and morality, questioning his past actions and desires. The chapter explores illusions versus reality, aesthetic obsession, and the tension between personal desire and conscience in Dorian’s Victorian world.

partialText: Private aviation sector is increasingly embracing digital currencies. Transacta delivers payment solutions for merchants handling large, complex deals. The partnership will improve payment speed, settlement reliability, and geographic coverage.

title: Vibe Coding vs Specs: The Missing Middle
partialText: Vibe coding is too reactive. Spec Driven Development is too heavy. I tried to find the middle ground by letting GPT-5.3 Codex plan its own architecture before writing code — and it mostly worked, but nobody has a name for this approach yet.

title: Ship First, Scale Never: Marvin’s Anti-Overengineering Guide
partialText: You have zero users and a 12-service microarchitecture. The repos that make money run SQLite on one server for under €10/month. The repos with Kubernetes have READMEs. Ship the boring thing. Scale when the problems are real and not rehearsed.

title: Beat the Spinner: Optimistic UI for LangGraph.js Agents
partialText: Eliminate the “spinning loader” pain: learn optimistic UI updates for LangGraph.js agents, plus rollback patterns and a TypeScript example.

title: Qwen3.5-9B: A Small Model With a Massive Context Window
partialText: Qwen3.5-9B is a compact vision-capable LLM with 262K native context, MoE efficiency, strong math/coding, and 201-language support.

title: RubricBench Exposes a Big Flaw in AI Grading
partialText: RubricBench measures how far AI-generated grading rubrics drift from human standards—and shows why automated evaluation can misfire.

title: Building a Scalable Price Pipeline for Trading Systems
partialText: Learn how to build a scalable price aggregation pipeline for trading systems. Covers dual-buffer design, columnar storage with ClickHouse, and real-time streaming architecture for OHLCV bar data.

title: Visualize 1,000 Earnings Reactions—Fast
partialText: Use FMP APIs to pull earnings, surprises, and price reactions across ~1,000 NASDAQ stocks—then tell the story with six trading visuals.

title: Building a SaaS With Zero Human Code
partialText: OpenLoop is a live feedback platform built almost entirely by autonomous AI agents—widget, roadmap, voting, admin, and all. Cost: ~$15.

title: Why “Write Faster Code” Is the Wrong Career Strategy Now
partialText: AI can write code fast. The new developer advantage is writing clear specs and guiding agents to build coherent systems.

title: Orpheus — an Open-source Edge AI Platform for Cross-species Communication Research
partialText: Orpheus is an autonomous research station in the Michigan woods running edge inference on NVIDIA Jetson — four cameras, four research-grade microphones, no cloud. It monitors wildlife, identifies birds, tracks corvid vocalizations, and is slowly learning to talk back.

title: Cloud Commitment Insurance Explained
partialText: Archera is a cloud commitment insurance service. It lets you lock in a service for a certain period of time and get a steep discount. But when things change, you’re left paying for servers nobody’s using. Archera lets you have both: savings and flexibility.

title: What This Weekend's Iran Crisis Actually Taught us About Price Action
partialText: Markets didn't drop because of Iran. They dropped because overleveraged positions got liquidated into thin weekend liquidity. The recovery came when forced selling exhausted and conviction buyers stepped in. Structure, not headlines.

title: What I've Learned Doing Vibe Coding
partialText: What Vibe Coding teached me and why fundamentals are still important today more than ever.

title: The Zomato API Bug That Turns Phone Numbers Into Location Intel
partialText: Zomato’s “Friend Recommendations” API allows unilateral contact syncing. By uploading a phone number, bad actors can extract a user’’ restaurant recommendation history and restaurant coordinates. By mapping overlapping delivery radii, an attacker can estimate a user's approximate physical location without their consent.

title: Humans Are Autocomplete Machines Too
partialText: The scariest lie isn’t AI hype—it’s “you can dream anything.” Humans remix experience; LLMs remix data. The gap is shrinking.
